summary: Richard A. Rosengarten is a scholar in religious studies. He has served at the University of Chicago as Dean (attested 2008–2012) and as Associate Professor of Religion and Literature, including in the College (attested 2026).
Richard B. Mahoney works in Buddhist and computational studies. He completed his MA at the University of Canterbury by 2002 under supervisor Paul Harrison, and held a post there attested in 2001.
Richard B. Martin worked in Tibetology and Indology. He held posts at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and as a South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

Richard Baker (born 1936) is a religious and Buddhist studies figure. He studied at UC Berkeley and Harvard, and under Shunryu Suzuki from 1961, whom he succeeded in 1971 as Abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center until 1984.
Richard Barron is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul III.

Richard Bowring (born 1947) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA, doctorate, and Litt.D at Cambridge, taught at Columbia and Princeton, served as Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012), and became Emeritus Professor at Cambridge in 1985.

Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) studied at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, and worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited the Indian Antiquary (~1884–1931), and was vice-president of the Hakluyt Society (~1928–1931).
Richard D. Mann is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003).

Richard D. McBride II works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued graduate studies at UCLA, was mentored by Robert E. Buswell Jr., held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis, and held a post at Dongguk University (attested 2012).

Richard Delbrueck (1875–1957) was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Bonn (~1893–1897). He held posts at Bonn (~1902–1908), Jena as Professor of Archaeology (~1911–1928), and Giessen (~1928–1940).

Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago by 2004 and held assistant (attested 2013) and associate (attested 2026) professorships in religious studies at Indiana University Bloomington.

Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Kiel University (~1885–1888). He worked at Kiel University Library, Berlin State Library, and served as director of Göttingen State and University Library while at the University of Göttingen (1921–1932).

Richard Foltz (born 1961) works in Iranian, religious, and historical studies. He studied at the University of Utah and Harvard (PhD ~1996), taught at Kuwait, Brown, Columbia, and Florida, and became Founding Director of Concordia University's Centre for Iranian Studies (~2006–2026).
Richard Fritzsche (born 1851) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus between ~1873 and 1877. He served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg (attested 1976).

Richard G. Salomon works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied under Ludo Rocher (~1970–1975) and served as a professor at the University of Washington from ~1981, becoming Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit in ~2019.

Richard Gombrich (born 1937) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his BA and DPhil at Oxford, the latter under R. C. Zaehner, and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College from 1965/1976 to 2004.

Richard Hartshorne (1899–1992) studied at Princeton University (~1916–1920) and the University of Chicago (~1920–1924). He held posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940–1970).

Richard Hauschild (1901–1972) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Jena, where he completed his doctorate (1926) and Habilitation (1948). He taught at the University of Jena as Lektor (1938) and Professor (1951–1967).

Richard Henebry (1863–1916) was a linguist. He studied at St. John's College, St Patrick's Pontifical University, and the universities of Greifswald and Freiburg, studying under Heinrich Zimmer between ~1895 and ~1898.

Richard Hugh Robinson (1926–1970) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Alberta, SOAS, and London under supervisors Arthur Waley and David Friedman, served on the Toronto faculty, and became a professor at Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.
